rationale:
Evidence: iteration 1 (score 33.89) is the best race so far. It used kp 3.0 with weights [-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1], base_speed 1.5, kd 0.03, ki 0.1 and wheel_track 0.12, and it gave the best oval progress (0.176). Iteration 2 (score 26.36) changed several values at once and lost progress, so it does not show that the revision helped. All designs left the line on every track, with max_error about 0.061 and steering_oscillation of 0.06 to 0.14. This points to a start or initial-alignment problem and to too little correction at the first bend, not to jitter.

What I kept from the critique: (a) kd 0.1 is too large. Its edge kick of about 5 turn units exceeds the proportional term, so I return kd to 0.03, the value used in iteration 1. (b) The integral needs to be tested, so ki rises. I set ki 0.5, which gives a maximum contribution of 1.0 turn units under the plus or minus 2 cap, enough to test bias removal without the 0.8 to 1.0 values that the critique says could saturate early. (c) base_speed 1.5 is kept because the best oval progress came at that speed. Completion is not expected at this speed.

What I rejected: I did not keep the revision's kp 1.5 or base_speed 1.0. The proportional gain of 1.5 per unit signal (kp 1.5 with weights of plus or minus 1) gave less progress than the kp 3.0 used in iteration 1, and the speed cut was not supported by data. I also reverted wheel_track from 0.14 to 0.12. The revision changed wheel_track without a test of its own, so 0.12 is the better-tested baseline.

Changes from iteration 1: only ki changes, from 0.1 to 0.5. This isolates whether a stronger integral removes the motor-mismatch bias. Expected (hypothesis): progress at least 0.18 on the oval and max_error at or below 0.061 m. If max_error stays at about 0.061 with the same early line-loss timing, the cause is the start, and the next revision should change initial alignment or line_loss handling. If rms_error rises with low steering_oscillation, the bias is the cause and ki should rise further. If steering_oscillation rises, lower kp first.
